question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 15 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 27 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 10 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM of given hours: LCM(15, 27, 10) = 270 units.

Combined efficiency of A, B, and C = (270 ÷ 15) + (270 ÷ 27) + (270 ÷ 10) = 18 + 10 + 27 = 55 units/hour.

Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency = 270 ÷ 55 hours.

On simplifying: 270 ÷ 55 = 54 ÷ 11 = 4 ¹⁰⁄₁₁ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 ¹⁰⁄₁₁ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A = 15 hours

Time taken by pipe B = 27 hours

Time taken by pipe C = 10 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

Time Taken Together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of pipes (A + B + C) = 18 + 10 + 27 = 55 units/hour

⇒ Time taken when operating together = Total Work ÷ Total efficiency

⇒ Time = 270 ÷ 55

⇒ Time = 54 ÷ 11 = 4 ¹⁰⁄₁₁ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 ¹⁰⁄₁₁ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Emptying Pipes (Negative Efficiency)

If a pipe empties a full tank in 'y' hours, its efficiency is taken as negative. When combining with a filling pipe, the net efficiency = (1 ÷ x) − (1 ÷ y).

Alternate Working of Pipes

When pipes are opened in alternate hours, calculate the combined work done in 1 cycle (e.g., 2 hours for 2 pipes). Multiply by the closest whole number factor before dealing with the remainder.

Actual Capacity of Tank

If the filling or emptying rate is given (e.g., liters per minute), the exact volume can be found by: Capacity = Time required to fill the tank × Rate of flow.
